mainEntity.name: How much does a Renault Clio 1.5 dCi engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement engine for a Renault Clio 1.5 dCi typically costs £900-£2,800 for the supply-only unit. Fitting adds 6-10 hours of labour at £65-£90/hr, bringing the total fitted cost to £1,500-£3,500 at an independent specialist. Dealer pricing is significantly higher.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of injector failure in a Renault Clio 1.5 dCi?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common signs are rough idle, hard starting, loss of power, excess smoke from the exhaust, and the engine warning light illuminating. On early K9K models (pre-2011), injector failure is often caused by metal swarf from a failing Delphi high-pressure fuel pump.

mainEntity.name: Is the Renault Clio 1.5 dCi a reliable engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 1.5 dCi has a double personality - some units exceed 300,000 km without issue, while others suffer serious failures. Pre-2011 models are more prone to injector and timing belt issues, while post-2011 models are significantly more robust. Regular maintenance is the key to longevity.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Renault Clio 1.5 dCi?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the vehicle's value. Clio II examples are worth £500-£2,000 - a full engine replacement at £1,800-£2,800 may exceed the car's value. Clio III examples (£1,000-£4,000) may justify replacement if the rest of the car is in good condition. Clio IV/Clio V examples with higher values (£3,000-£10,000) generally justify replacement.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the K9K 628 and K9K 638 engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The K9K 628 produces 75PS (55kW) and was fitted to Clio IV models from 2012-2019. The K9K 638 produces 90PS (66kW) and was also fitted to Clio IV models from 2012-2019. Both share the same 1.5-litre (1,461cc) displacement and the same K9K architecture, but the 638 is the higher-output version.

mainEntity.name: Does the Renault Clio 1.5 dCi have a timing belt or chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 1.5 dCi (K9K) uses a timing belt, not a chain. The belt requires replacement at the manufacturer-recommended interval - typically every 60,000 miles or 5 years, whichever comes sooner. Neglecting the timing belt can lead to catastrophic engine failure if it breaks.

historyTimeline.h2: Renault Clio 1.5 dCi - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Renault Clio 1.5 dCi, powered by the legendary K9K engine, has been the backbone of Renault's diesel range for over two decades. First introduced in the Clio II in 2001, this 1.5-litre turbo diesel became one of Europe's most popular and widely produced small-capacity diesel engines. Fitted to every generation of Clio from II through to V, the K9K family offers power outputs from 65PS to 110PS. While generally reliable when maintained, early examples have well-documented injector, timing belt and bearing issues that make replacement a common consideration for high-mileage owners.

milestones.description: 2005 (Clio II) - Early K9K 1.5 dCi introduced (65PS/75PS); common-rail direct injection; 8-valve and 16-valve variants
2012 (Clio III) - K9K 764, K9K 774, K9K 766 (78PS) and other variants; Euro 4 emissions
2011 - Timing belt failures reported on some K9K units; Renault addressed with revised components
2019 (Clio IV) - K9K 612 (75PS), K9K 628 (75PS), K9K 629 (90PS), K9K 638 (90PS); Euro 5 and Euro 6 compliance; DPF fitted
2019 (Clio IV facelift) - Continued K9K production with updated emissions systems
present (Clio V) - K9K 872 (85PS Blue dCi); latest Euro 6d-TEMP compliance

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Renault Clio 1.5 dCi is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Renault Clio 1.5 dCi Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Renault Clio 1.5 dCi (K9K family) is one of Europe's most popular diesel engines, but it has several well-documented failure points. The 1.5 dCi has a "double personality" - some units exceed 300,000 km without issue, while others suffer serious failures. Rebuilt engines supplied through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Injector Failure - Delphi Pump Swarf and Injector Wear in the Renault Clio 1.5 dCi
problems.affectedModels: Renault Clio 1.5 dCi (K9K, particularly pre-2011 models)
problems.rootCause: Early K9K engines (pre-2011) suffer from a known issue where the Delphi high-pressure fuel pump wears prematurely, producing metal swarf (particles) that contaminates the entire fuel system. This swarf damages injectors, the fuel rail, and the pump itself. Injector wear is also common on later models.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New injectors, fuel system flush, new fuel filter
repairOptions.longevity: Cost-effective if caught before pump swarf has contaminated the entire system

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt unit with upgraded components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if pump failure has caused widespread fuel system contamination or engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Apply this UK-wide decision framework to your Renault Clio 1.5 dCi. Clio II examples typically range £500-£2,000; Clio III examples range £1,000-£4,000; Clio IV/Clio V examples range £3,000-£10,000. - Vehicle worth under ~£2,000: used engine typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit - or consider scrapping if repair costs exceed value - Vehicle worth ~£2,000-£5,000: evaluate both; injector replacement is viable if the car is otherwise sound - Vehicle worth £5,000+: reconditioned/rebuilt usually justifies the premium via warranty and reliability
problems.recommendation: If your Clio 1.5 dCi has rough running, hard starting or loss of power, have the injectors and fuel pump inspected immediately. Early injector replacement costs £500-£900 at a specialist. Ignoring the issue risks widespread fuel system contamination and a £1,800-£2,800 engine replacement bill.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt Renault Clio 1.5 dCi engine prices

problems.h4: Timing Belt Failure - The K9K's Critical Weak Point (2009-2011)
problems.rootCause: Between 2009 and 2011, some K9K engines suffered from timing belt misalignment issues, causing premature belt wear and, in some cases, belt breakage. If the belt breaks, the engine suffers catastrophic valve-to-piston contact, requiring a full rebuild or replacement.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New timing belt, tensioner, water pump
repairOptions.longevity: Essential preventative maintenance every 60,000 miles or 5 years

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt unit with upgraded components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if belt has broken and caused valve/piston damage

problems.recommendation: Timing belt replacement is the single most important maintenance item on the Clio 1.5 dCi. If your car is approaching 60,000 miles or is over 5 years old, have the belt replaced immediately. A £300-£500 preventative job is far cheaper than a £1,800-£2,800 engine replacement.
problems.cta: -> Compare Renault Clio 1.5 dCi engine replacement costs

problems.h4: EGR Valve & DPF Clogging - Emissions System Failures in the Renault Clio 1.5 dCi
problems.affectedModels: Renault Clio 1.5 dCi (all K9K, particularly Euro 5/6 models with DPF)
problems.rootCause: EGR valve clogging is one of the most common diesel problems on the Clio 1.5 dCi, causing rough idle, poor fuel economy and engine hesitation. DPF clogging is also common, especially on vehicles used primarily for short urban journeys.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Professional EGR valve cleaning or removal
repairOptions.longevity: Cost-effective first-line response for rough idle and hesitation
Effective if DPF is not heavily blocked

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New EGR valve and associated gaskets
repairOptions.longevity: Required if cleaning does not resolve the issue

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt unit with upgraded components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Only if emissions system failure has caused turbo or engine damage

problems.recommendation: If your Clio 1.5 dCi is used primarily for short journeys, ensure it gets regular motorway runs to keep the DPF healthy. If the EGR valve is clogged, professional cleaning is a cost-effective solution - but if the DPF warning appears, act quickly; a forced regeneration is far cheaper than a full replacement.
